chapter: Vidals, blues, teachers and the Silver Leaf band
title: The Silver Leaf photograph and its members
summary: They look at the photo and Charles names Winnie Carter, Philip Nixon, Sam Dutrey, Albert Baptiste and Jim Johnson.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now we've got this picture of the Silver Leaf here. I think this is in Sam Charles' book. You know, he put that in the book. I don't know if you know that or not.

I don't know. I gave him the picture. Yeah, well anyhow. Even the one when I was taking music lessons. You remember the small one was in there? I had a small one in there. I didn't see that. You didn't see the small one in the one I was taking lessons? Uh-uh. Let me see if I can find it.
Alright, I'll just turn the machine on. Oh, that uniform. 1912, 1913. 1913 he bought those uniforms.
I see. That was a Silver Leaf band. I have a feeling that he has a lot more photographs back in there. Oh, that's beautiful. You got your music there in your case.
That's right. Your music rack with music on it. But in that Silver Leaf band, who was in it when you first showed up? I was in it. I was in it.
The first one was in it when you first joined. But in that Silver Leaf band, who was in it when you first joined?

The first one was in it, but the first one was just that bunch that you see in there with the exception of the trombone is not there. That was Dutray's brother, Noray Dutray. Honoré Dutray was his name. Besides that, that was the whole band. Those days we didn't use piano hardly. That's the way all those bands were. They didn't hardly use any piano.
Well who are those people in the picture? There's a drummer.
Winnie Carter. Philip Nixon, Samuel Dutray, Albert Baptiste. Albert Baptiste? That's right. Philip Nixon and Jim Johnson.
Now that was the men all the way through until you quit the band? Until it broke up?

Until it broke up there, that's right. You just had substitutes once in a while. Well we had to, because many times some fellas couldn't play on it. And not even saying that, some of them, they wouldn't leave their work to come and play music because like I tell you, they didn't pay. They just didn't pay, that's all. Every in a while I wouldn't leave the bank. They were playing those night club where all them fellas was playing in the district they called it. They claimed they was making all that money but I was afraid. I thought probably might be just like all the rest of the work. There's something that I wanted to ask you
